title: Timing a roast dinner
lede: Everything has to reach the table hot at the same moment. Work out when each thing starts.
intent: Learners can work backwards from a serving time to decide when each part of a multi-part meal must start.
goal: work backwards from a serving time to decide when each part of a meal must start.
prompt: Dinner is served 105 minutes after you start. At what minute should each task begin?

items.label: Lamb into the oven
items.why: A 1.5 kg leg needs about 90 minutes, then 15 minutes resting. That rest is why it goes in first.

items.label: Parboil the potatoes
items.why: About twelve minutes in boiling water, then a few minutes to steam dry before they hit the fat.

items.label: Potatoes into the oven
items.why: About 45 minutes to crisp. They share the oven with the lamb for its last half hour.

items.label: Lamb out to rest
items.why: Resting lets the juices settle back through the meat. Carve straight away and they run onto the board.

items.label: Make the gravy
items.why: Made in the roasting tin from the pan juices, so it cannot start until the lamb comes out.

items.label: Steam the beans
items.why: Green vegetables go on last. They lose colour and bite within minutes of being cooked.

teach.watchFor: Learners timing forwards from the start instead of backwards from service. Ask them to begin with the last thing on the plate.

sources.label: Cooking times written for this activity
sources.note: Check the times against your kitchen's recipes and equipment.
